I already had a similar case (the Aerb brand), so I can compare the two directly.New Trent superior on the following points:- The rotation is butter-smooth, even right out of the box. I don't quite understand the 60-degree position lock, but it's no biggie. Just a little strange since I can't imagine what I'd use that kind of iPad position for.- The metal stand adjustment is very smooth as well. I had no trouble taking out the iPad stand and putting it back into the keyboard. I can see this being important when I'm traveling and have to use it at weird angles.- Buttons are more robust.- The case stays closed with the little rubber lock strap. The Aerb doesn't have that, but it has a similar magnetic lock/unlock so there have been times when I've run down the iPad's battery because it was stored upright and case was cracked open.- The automatic Bluetooth reconnection is very nice as well. When I don't want to drain the keyboard's battery and turn it off, I can simply turn the Bluetooth back on and it will reconnect. Nice touch!- The backspace key is where it usually is on a regular keyboard. For the Aerb case, the "Lock iPad" key is where the backspace key usually is, and I've locked my iPad a billion times by accident, when I wanted to delete something.Aerb superior on the following points:- The existence of a "Delete" key. For the Aerb case, you can delete by using the function key with the lock key, but I tried that with the New Trent and it didn't work. It's a small thing, but I'd like that.- "Right where I left it" screen unlocking from the keyboard. With the Aerb, if I accidentally press the lock key, I can press it again within a few seconds and the screen will be back exactly to what it was without having to slide right to unlock. On the New Trent, when I have accidentally pressed the lock key, when I press it again to turn the screen back on, I have to unlock the iPad manually from the screen.Clearly, New Trent wins! One remedy, add more grinds to the Aeropress for a stronger brew and then dilute the result to taste with hot water.Clean-up is a cinch, an easy quick rinse. reviewText: I'm very happy with the 2015 version of the Roku 2.  It is easy to use, the performance is very snappy, the menus are fluid and the menu system and navigation is so intuitive that most people will never need a manual or any tech support.Setup is also easy:  connect it to your HDTV or home theater receiver using an HDMI cable (not included, but you can one cheap on Amazon), plug in the power adapter, and follow the on-screen instructions.  It's so easy, my parents could do it.  As with Blu Ray players, the HDMI cable carries both the video and audio signals.  The Roku's picture and sound quality are very good on my modest system (though, like all other streaming boxes, picture and sound from internet streaming are not quite up to par with the best Blu Ray discs).The included remote is nicely designed and is much easier to use than the remotes that came with my TV and Blu Ray players.  However, as an "IR" type remote, it requires a direct line of sight to the Roku box, so you can't hide the Roku box in a cabinet, it has to be out in the open.  The Roku 2 comes with Duracell batteries for the remote, which should last for years.  (The batteries that came with my last Roku box in 2011 lasted until 2014.)If you have an iPhone or Android phone, you can use your phone as a remote using a free app from Roku.  Doing this can come in handy.  If you want to enter text using the Roku remote, for example to search for a movie or to set up your Netflix account, you have to move the cursor to each letter and select it; this is a bit tedious.  Using the smartphone app, you can pull up an on-screen keyboard and type text in directly; it's quicker and easier.  Also, the latest version of the Roku smartphone app has voice search:  just say the name of the movie you want, and it will show you all the channels that has that movie, then touch the one you want and it'll take you right there.  If you misplace your Roku remote or the batteries die and you don't have replacements handy, it's nice to be able to use your phone as the remote.  And lastly, you don't need a direct line of sight to control your Roku box with the smartphone app, because the app uses your wifi network rather than infrared.The alternatives to Roku are Amazon Fire TV and Apple TV.  All three platforms have their advantages and disadvantages. Apple TV is the only one you can use to view content from the iTunes store, and it can also mirror content from your iPhone or iPad if you have one.  But the Apple TV hasn't been updated in years and is overdue for a new version (hence its recent price drop).  Amazon Fire TV is great if you have a Kindle Fire tablet; Amazon Fire TV also has voice search which works great for searching for content available from Amazon.  Roku has the most channels of all of them and is my favorite.  But all three platforms have their loyal fans.If you choose the Roku platform, you can buy this Roku 2 or the Roku 3 for $30 more.  The 2015 versions of the Roku 2 and Roku 3 offer identical performance; the only difference is the remote:  The remote that comes with the Roku 3 has an earphone jack, a motion sensor for playing games on the Roku, and a mic for voice search.  For me, these extra features are not worth the extra $30.  But they will be for some people.If you have an older Roku (I did), the 2015 updated Roku 2 will be a big step up in performance.  It's really easy and fast to use, and navigating the menus is super easy and intuitive.  If you've never used a streaming box, the Roku platform is a really excellent one, almost no learning curve and well designed with just about everything you could want from a streaming box.One last caution:  The Roku 2 and 3 were originally introduced 2 years ago.  These 2015 updated versions are very good, especially the 2015 Roku 2.  But this is not a fundamentally new device.  Roku is likely to come out with a "Roku 4" later this year that will offer 4K resolution, faster performance, and probably some other new features.  If you don't have a 4K TV, the 2015 Roku 2 is a really great option.The other reviewer has a less favorable perspective and you should read his/her review before spending your hard-earned money.  But my experience with the new Roku 2 is very positive and I recommend it highly.

Amazon's vine program regularly offers me this type of vaguely healthy, vaguely sugary snacks.  Sometimes I accept.  Usually, I am disappointed.  These things, though, are actually pretty good.  They are described as dark chocolate, nuts, and sea salt.  That's pretty much what you taste.  The strongest flavor components are the nuts, which are very lightly salted with sea salt.  So, you taste the nuts, not the salt.  On top of that, they use dark chocolate, but in relatively small quantities so that the nuts remain the primary flavor component.  The fact that they use dark chocolate keeps the bars from being too sweet, and the light amount of sea salt is just enough for the nuts without overpowering anything.  I hate healthy snacks that try to mimic candy bars.  Such attempts generally use poor quality chocolate in large quantities, and usually wind up with about as many calories per gram as normal candy bars anyway.  These bars, though, just taste like what they are.  If you want a snickers bar with fewer calories, you are out of luck.  However, if you like nuts that are very lightly salted, dark chocolate, and don't want something as sweet as a candy bar, these are actually pretty good.

This steam mop really lives up to the claims.  It gets my floor very clean, and when left sitting on hard stains for a bit, brings them up with no problems.  I have treated wood floors in half of my house, and so it takes quite a few fills to get it all done, but that's understandable for the compact size of the unit.it's easy enough to use that my 12 and 8 year old daughters can help out with the floors with a little supervision.  I've read some reviews that state that sometimes it steams too much and gets the floor too wet.  This is true, but I find that when that happens it rectifies itself after about one tank full has gone through it.  Holding it sideways for a couple minutes seems to also help clear up this problem.I'm really psyched about having NO chemicals on my floor, and NO sticky residue.  If you do get a sticky residue, it means you waited too long to do your floors, and you simply need to rinse the cloth and do them again.The only problem is that the cloths do shrink.  I found that after a few uses they are harder to get the bottom covered, so you have to be careful not to scratch your floor.  If you're not marathon cleaning this isn't a problem though.  I'm going to see if I can buy larger pads for it, but these still work just fine.I've tried a lot of steam mops and chemical mops, and this one is a real keeper.  I'm very glad I bought it, and if it ever dies (perish the thought!) I will certainly purchase another.

I read reviews of hard surface floor cleaners on many sites before purchasing the Eureka.  I am very pleased with the performance of this steamer.  I have a linoleum floor in my kitchen and hardwood floors in many other rooms.  When you weigh it against mopping with a bucket of water and sponge mop, I think it has several advantages.  Firstly, the steam.  It takes off tacky pieces effortlessly after just holding the steamer over the area for 5-10 seconds.  Even with my old mop that had a scrub brush on the reverse side for such tasks, sometimes I needed to still get down on my hands and knees to remove them.  The steamer does it with out bending over.  The steamer is not heavy, but has enuf weight to it that you don't need to scrub back and forth over the same area.  In fact, moving slowing section by section is the best way to a clean floor.  At first, I felt like the task was slower, but when you consider that the floor is dry almost instantly, you aren't waiting 20 minutes for the floor to dry before you can walk on it (which is big with 3 kids who are constantly around).  I have even found it relaxing since you aren't bending over pushing the mop back and forth and wringing it out constantly.  It also gets right up to my baseboards.  When using the steamer on my hardwood floors, I move the steamer along quicker so the drying is instantaneous.  Overall, I believe my floors are cleaner with less work!!  The only reason I did not give it 5 stars is that I had anticipated it maneuvering much like my swiffer to get around the toilet.  It does move and twist rather easily, but the bottom of the steamer seems a little big to get in the tighest spot around the toilet.  That's my only complaint, but not much of one when one swipe of a clorox wipe can take care of that area.

I'll start out by saying that we have two large and hairy dogs and that when they come into the house, it's directly into the kitchen, no luxurious mud room, etc.  Luckily we have a porcelain tile floor, and it's a great color.  But still, who wants to feel that grit under your feet?This mop does an adequate job.  I vacuum the floor first to get up the doggy debris and then use the mop.  As many other reviewers have said, the steam lasts long enough for a "normal sized" kitchen.  Ours is not large, and there's usually enough steam to hit parts of the dining room, too.  It's 70 year old oak, so I don't let the steamer sit in one spot, just go over it lightly, and it does a nice job.I like the fact that this mop doesn't use any chemicals.  The hot steam is enough to get up any dried food spills that are on the floor.  Still, I've always used vinegar & water, and I'm missing that sense of clean, so sometimes I spritz the floor first and then use the steam mop.  That gives the vinegar action w/o it going through the steamer, since the directions say not to use vinegar.  Another tip--wet the cloth before you attach it to the steamer.  Otherwise you use up too much steam just getting it thoroughly wet.  I've tried this a couple of times now, and I like the results.  As to washing and drying the cloths, I do put them right in the washer and dryer and they have not shrunk.  They're very sturdy so should last a long time.Why only 4 stars?  I like the steamer.  It's easy to use and does get up a lot of the dirt.  But it doesn't get the floor spotlessly clean.  After I wash it, if I wipe a spot with a clean paper towel, the towel will still look kind of dirty.  Nothing's as good as being on your hands and knees and really washing the floor.  But I've got better things to do these days, so this is fine.

The Good1) It's fun and works well once setup.2) After it's finally connected to the network adding the bulb to other devices was quite easy.  (installed on Android devices)3) The alarm feature works great! I've set mine to gradually increase in brightness and then eventually just turn itself off.4) The bulb has neat transition and strobe effects if you're into that sort of thing.5) It can work remotely without you being in the house if you configure it to work that way.6) Some reviewers have complained on Google Play that there isn't a widget that can be used on Android.  There is a widget now and it works well.7) Brightness is about what you would expect from a bulb like this.8) The application supports more than one bulb and you can create groups if you want to control them together.9) Comes with a 2 year warranty if you register online.The Bad1) It doesn't work on 5 GHz and the documentation doesn't tell you that. My setup failed and I had to read through the help section of the app to figure out what was going on. Then I had to factory reset the bulb and start over. The setup should tell you this in advance.  I could see someone that's not really technically inclined getting a little frustrated.  They may not even know what frequency their access point is even running on.The Indifferent1) App design is a little dated on Android.  Although it was recently updated it doesn't really follow the Android Material Design guidelines.  The app is still functional and works fine.  I'm just being a little nitpicky.2) This is a stand alone Wi-Fi device only (not Z-Wave or ZigBee). Currently, at the time of this review, it doesn't integrate with Tasker, IFTTT, or any other application or service.The Bottom LineLet's be real here.  This bulb doesn't have the full functionality of a Hue bulb system but you're also not paying the hefty price of a Hue system either.  This is a great option to get into the color LED game.  If Flux could refine the setup process to include only 2.4 GHz access points or have the bulb support 5 GHz (better option) it would turn the only negative into a positive. I bought the bulb to use as a wake-up light now that fall is nearly here and it works fantastic in this regard.  Everything else was just a bonus.
